c1-45.title: Writing a Novel
c1-45.story: Anna has secretly been working on her first novel all autumn. Late one night she printed the whole [[manuscript]] and handed it to Max, who reads more than anyone she knows. He started with the [[prologue]], in which a lighthouse keeper finds a letter washed up on the shore. "Your [[protagonist]] is wonderful," he said, "but that line about a dark and stormy night is a [[cliché]]." Anna laughed and admitted the opening was an [[homage]] to the old adventure books her grandpa used to read to her. Max's favorite part was the keeper's long [[monologue]] to the sea, which he read aloud twice. He asked whether she planned to turn it into a family [[saga]] covering three generations. Anna said she might, but only if she could publish it under a [[pseudonym]]. "That way, if it flops, nobody at university will know," she joked. Max promised to keep her secret and asked for chapter two by Friday.

c1-46.title: The Charity Gala
c1-46.story: Lisa's aunt was organizing a [[gala]] to raise money for a children's hospital in Kyiv, and she invited Anna and Ira to help. She has worked as a professional [[fundraiser]] for years, so she knew exactly how to fill a ballroom. The theme was the 1920s, and the evening opened with a playful [[burlesque]] act full of feathers and silly jokes. Then the host took the stage, and his [[charisma]] had the whole room laughing within minutes. Behind a white screen, a dancer's [[silhouette]] moved to soft jazz while guests placed their bids. A local reporter was hoping for an [[exclusive]] with the hospital's head doctor, who had flown in that afternoon. By midnight, the [[fundraising]] total was twice what anyone had expected. The doctor announced that part of the money would go into an [[endowment]] to support the children's ward for years to come. Anna and Ira were exhausted, but they agreed it was the best Saturday they'd had in ages.

c1-47.title: An Evening Language Class
c1-47.story: This semester Anna signed up for an evening course in [[Hindi]], mostly because she loves Indian films. Her teacher, Mr. Rao, is wonderfully [[old-school]]: he writes everything on a chalkboard and never uses slides. On the first night, he explained that many words in the language go back to [[Sanskrit]], which is over three thousand years old. Max, who had joined just to keep her company, asked whether learning it would sharpen his [[intellect]]. "Only if you actually do your homework," the teacher replied, with a hint of [[sarcasm]] that made everyone laugh. Later, they read a short newspaper article and discussed how political [[discourse]] differs between India and Ukraine. By the end of the evening, Max could write his own name and was surprisingly proud of himself. He has already asked Anna twice when the next class is.

c1-48.title: Greek Letters in Math
c1-48.story: Taras came home from school confused by the strange symbols in his geometry homework. Anna sat down with him and explained that mathematicians often borrow Greek letters to name angles. "This one is [[alpha]], the first letter, and this one is [[gamma]], the third," she said. Taras thought the third one looked like a little slingshot and drew one in the margin. To make it more fun, Anna showed him a map of the Danube [[delta]], which spreads out like a triangle where the river meets the Black Sea. Next, he had to find the [[perimeter]] of a rectangular garden, which was easy once he stopped staring at the letters. Meanwhile, Max was testing the [[beta]] of a new homework app and offered to let Taras try it. His message ended with an [[acronym]] Taras didn't know, so Anna explained that "BTW" means "by the way." Before bed, Taras announced that [[omega]], the last letter, was now his favorite, because it meant homework was over.

c1-49.title: At the Nature Reserve
c1-49.story: Max's sister Sofia is spending the summer volunteering at a nature reserve in western Canada, and on Sunday she video-called the whole group. She had just watched a [[grizzly]] fishing for salmon in the river below the lodge. Earlier that week, a ranger had spotted a [[cougar]] near the main trail, so visitors now have to hike in pairs. Further north, she said, a herd of [[caribou]] passes through every autumn on its long migration. The reserve also protects a small band of wild horses, and her favorite is a gray [[mustang]] she has named Smoke. In the visitor center there is a sad display about the [[dodo]], a reminder of what happens when people ignore endangered species. A volunteer from Australia keeps comparing everything to the [[dingo]] back home, which Sofia finds hilarious. Last weekend they took a boat along the coast and watched an [[albatross]] glide for an hour without flapping once. The only real drama so far came from a tourist who tried to sneak in a [[chihuahua]] in her handbag. "Honestly," Sofia laughed, "the bears were calmer than that dog."

c1-50.title: A Strange Biology Seminar
c1-50.story: In Thursday's biology seminar, Lisa's professor set out to prove that nature is stranger than any movie. She began with the ocean, where tiny drifting [[plankton]] feed some of the largest whales on Earth. Then she played a video of a [[gibbon]] swinging through the rainforest at incredible speed. Lisa was amazed to learn that every [[primate]], from lemurs to humans, shares a large number of genes. Next came a less charming topic: a [[parasite]] that can change the behavior of the ant it lives in. Ants, she explained, normally leave a [[pheromone]] trail for the rest of the colony to follow. To finish, she asked each student to choose an island and research its native [[flora]] and [[fauna]] for next week. Lisa picked Madagascar, mainly because she wanted an excuse to watch more lemur videos.

c1-51.title: Farming and the Land
c1-51.story: Last summer Anna spent a week on her grandparents' farm, which sits on a windy [[plateau]] above the river. They grow sunflowers and wheat on about forty [[acres|acre]], and they keep three cows as well. Grandpa likes to joke that the cows produce more [[methane]] than a small factory. He has stopped using any [[pesticide]] on the fields, because he worries about the bees. Grandma, however, still keeps a small bottle of [[insecticide]] for the aphids on her roses. At dinner, everyone argued about a company that wanted to try [[fracking]] for gas a few miles away. Grandpa said no amount of money was worth risking the village wells. Anna changed the subject by describing a documentary about farmers in the Andes who grow [[coca]] for a traditional tea. Then Grandma handed her a jar of homemade hand cream with [[shea]] butter, saying farm work is hard on the skin. Anna went home with sunburned shoulders, soft hands, and a new respect for farmers.

c1-52.title: Hiring a New Team
c1-52.story: Ira's mom works in [[recruiting]] at a growing software company in Kyiv, and this month she has to hire an entire new team. The first person she needed was a [[sales manager]] who could win clients abroad. She also had to find a [[middle manager]] to sit between the founders and a dozen junior developers. Most candidates had impressive degrees, but the founders cared more about practical [[know-how]] than diplomas. One of them, a [[self-made]] entrepreneur who had once run a bakery, impressed everyone with his energy. In the final round, each candidate had to solve a real [[case study]] about a delayed product launch. The strongest answer came from a woman who had taught [[project management]] at a business school. Ira's mom had first heard her speak at a tech [[symposium]] in Lviv, where she gave the [[keynote]]. By Friday the team was complete, and Ira's mom celebrated with a very large pizza.
